title: The oil machine
hook: Where oil comes out of the ground, how it travels, and who burns it.

title: Pipes and ships
hook: Gas moves by pipeline or as a liquid on ships. Europe just switched from one to the other.

title: Who has what
hook: The metals in your phone and car, and the food on your plate, come from surprisingly few places.

title: Who owes whom
hook: The world's governments owe about $100 trillion. Here is where the debt sits and who lends it.

title: The map lies
hook: Greenland looks as big as Africa. It's fourteen times smaller.

title: Half the world in one circle
hook: More people live inside this circle than outside it.

title: The world in 2100
hook: Europe and East Asia are greying. Africa is young.

title: Who is in the dark
hook: One in ten people on Earth still has no electricity.

title: Chokepoints
hook: A handful of narrow straits carry the world's oil and goods.

title: Blocs over time
hook: Watch alliances grow, split and shift from 1945 to today.

title: Same border, different truths
hook: Every map takes a side. Here are six places where it shows.

title: The Arctic opens
hook: Melting ice is creating a new ocean, and new claims.

title: The internet is under the sea
hook: Almost all intercontinental data travels through cables on the seabed.

title: The economic centre of gravity
hook: For 2,000 years, the world's economic centre has been on the move.

title: Where your phone comes from
hook: Follow a smartphone from the mine to your pocket.

title: Critical minerals
hook: The energy transition runs on minerals from very few places.

title: Austria's gas
hook: How Austria ran on Siberian gas, then stopped.

title: Money sent home
hook: Migrants send home more than all foreign aid and investment combined.

title: One journey north
hook: From Caracas to the US border, through one of the world's most dangerous jungles.

title: What's on your plate
hook: A Viennese breakfast, traced back to its fields.

title: Why planes fly curves
hook: The straight line on a globe is a curve on a flat map.

title: Languages going quiet
hook: About 7,000 languages, and many have only a few speakers left.

title: Where people really live
hook: Country totals hide it: most of humanity is packed into river valleys, deltas and coasts.

title: A warming world
hook: Play 140 years of temperature records and watch the planet turn red, fastest at the top.

title: Rivers of air
hook: Ten kilometres up, winds of 200 km/h circle the planet. Planes ride them east.

title: Whose land?
hook: The same piece of land is drawn differently depending on who prints the map.

title: Inside the lines
hook: National averages hide big differences between a country's own regions.

title: Who emits the carbon
hook: Count carbon dioxide by country, by person or since 1850, and the ranking flips each time.

title: How long we live
hook: A child born today can expect to live about 73 years, nearly 30 more than in 1950. Not everywhere, and not in a straight line.

title: Clocks against the sun
hook: Noon on the clock should be when the sun is highest. In much of the world it isn't, and the date line zig-zags.

title: A World Cup across a continent
hook: The 2026 World Cup was spread over three countries, sixteen cities and four time zones. Qatar's fitted inside one city.

title: Votes for women
hook: New Zealand let women vote in 1893. Saudi Arabia did so in 2015. Watch the right spread, country by country.

title: The end of executions
hook: In 1977 only 16 countries had abolished the death penalty. Today 113 have. Watch them come, and see who still kills.

title: A world of new states
hook: Most of today's countries are younger than the United Nations. Watch them appear, wave after wave, from 1776 to 2011.

title: One sea, six claimants
hook: China claims most of the South China Sea. Its neighbours, and an international court, disagree.

title: Rivers across borders
hook: When a river crosses a border, whoever is upstream holds the tap. Three rivers show what happens next.

title: Where the boxes go
hook: All ten of the world's busiest container ports are in Asia, and six are in mainland China.

title: The burger standard
hook: A Big Mac costs $9 in Switzerland and under $2.50 in India. What the price of a burger says about money.

title: The nuclear club
hook: Nine countries have nuclear weapons. Four others once had them and gave them up.

title: America's bases abroad
hook: About 170,000 US troops serve abroad. Half of them are in just two countries.

title: The world votes on Ukraine
hook: In March 2022, 141 countries at the UN demanded that Russia leave Ukraine. Here is who did not, and how the vote has shifted since.

title: Sanctions and Russian oil
hook: About 50 governments imposed sanctions on Russia after it invaded Ukraine. Most of the world did not, and that is where Russia's oil went.

title: The great journeys
hook: A fleet that circled the Earth, a Chinese armada, and a traveller who walked half the known world.

title: The Silk Roads
hook: For 1,500 years, silk, paper, faith and plague moved across Asia along the same caravan tracks.

title: Out of Africa
hook: Every person alive descends from people who lived in Africa. Here is how, and roughly when, they reached the rest of the world.

title: How COVID-19 spread
hook: From one city in December 2019 to almost every country on Earth in three months.

title: Where the Earth breaks
hook: Every big earthquake since 1900 lies on a few narrow lines: the edges of the plates.

title: Counting war
hook: Researchers in Uppsala log every deadly clash they can verify. Here is what their records show for Ukraine, Syria and Sudan.

title: Borders through time
hook: Most of today's borders are younger than your grandparents. Watch empires break apart.

title: Liberation Day
hook: On 2 April 2025 the US put a tariff on almost every country, from 10% to 50%. Where the numbers came from, what actually applied, and what is left after the courts.

title: The China spiral
hook: In ten days of April 2025 the US and China raised tariffs on each other to 145% and 125%. How the spiral started, how it was unwound, and what rare earths had to do with it.

title: Steel, cars, chips
hook: One product at a time, the US has put national-security tariffs on metals, cars, wood, medicine and chips. Here is where those goods come from.

title: Deal or retaliate
hook: Faced with US tariffs, most countries negotiated, two hit back and a few were singled out for punishment. Who did what, and what it got them.

title: Tariffs on trial
hook: Small businesses sued, and the Supreme Court struck down the biggest tariffs of 2025. Within months, most of them were back under other laws.

title: Trade takes a detour
hook: Tariffs cut what America buys from China by almost half. The goods now come from Mexico, Taiwan, Vietnam and Thailand instead.

title: Who pays the tariffs
hook: US customs revenue quadrupled in 2025. The bill landed mostly on American companies and shoppers, and then a court ordered much of it paid back.

title: The deficit that would not shrink
hook: Tariffs were meant to close America's trade gap. The deficit with China shrank, but the overall gap barely moved: it shifted to Vietnam, Taiwan and Mexico.

title: Where the whales were
hook: Half a million noon positions from American whaling logbooks show a fleet that chased whales into every ocean, then collapsed.

title: The launch explosion
hook: For half a century the world launched 55 to 141 rockets a year. Since 2019 the number has more than tripled, and one company flies half of them.

title: All roads lead to Rome
hook: The Romans built about 300,000 km of roads, from Scotland to the Nile. A new atlas maps every one of them, and shows how few we can trace for certain.

title: How long were you a colony?
hook: Cape Verde spent more than 500 years under Portugal, Iraq 15 under Britain. How long European empires ruled each country, and who ruled.
